doc.title: George Masso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997

title: Younger trombonists and the changing instrument
summary: John Allred, Dan Barrett, Fontana, Watrous and Green and the microphone as extension of the trombone.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: I’ve seen in colleges and high schools that trombone players are getting a bit scarce. Have you seen that?

Yeah. I guess it’s true. I hear a lot about it, but I also hear about young trombone players coming up — very, very good players too. A case in point is John Allred, who is here at this festival. Excellent player with a lot of facility and he knows how to make music with it too.

Yeah. Dan Barrett is a colleague and a good friend and a marvelous player. I love playing with Dan because we work well off one another. And I mean there are even younger guys coming up out of the colleges who have a tremendous amount of facility and range. You know the instrument has changed so much over the last 30 or 40 years in that you know people like Carl Fontana and Bill Watrous and Urbie Green had such facility and inspired

an awful lot of these younger people I think to develop it. It’s a whole different approach to playing you know. I think the microphone becomes an extension of your instrument — a different approach. But I have a lot of respect for these guys that developed that.
